summary: ```markdown # 【Marvelous Designer】Learning Day - Swimwear Production p01 ## Introduction Hello, good evening everyone. My name is Sherry, and I'm a designer at Marvelous Designer. Today, I'm going to show you how to make a dress, specifically Hannah's dress, which is the theme of today's video. ## Drawing the Base First, we're going to use the 3D drawing function to draw a circle on the virtual model. Make sure to press the `Ctrl` key while drawing to create straight lines. We need to draw this circle as it will serve as a base for our design. After that, we will flatten this circle to ensure that the shape remains unchanged. ## Adding Fabric Once we have the circle flattened, we will add fabric on top of it. It's essential to arrange the fabric correctly in the 3D window. Next, we will use a tool called "Flatten" to prepare the template for further adjustments. ## Pinning and Simulation After creating the template, I will add pins to the two ends of the circle. This is crucial because the template may not perfectly match our model. Once we have everything set, we will turn on the simulation feature to see how the fabric behaves. ## Adjusting the Steel Ring To fit the chest line of our model, I will adjust the position of the steel ring. After making these adjustments, we can freeze the two panels we have created. These panels will serve as a basis for creating additional panels in between, which is particularly useful for swimsuits or tight clothing. ## Drawing Additional Panels Next, I will draw other panels following the body line of the virtual model. For tight outfits, we typically draw the basic panels directly on the model and then flatten them to check how many panels appear in the 2D window. ## Symmetrical Panel Creation After flattening, we will create symmetrical panels. Once we have the shape of the panel, we can start checking for alignment with the side panels. If there are any discrepancies, I will adjust the size accordingly. ## Layering and Sewing Lines After aligning the side panel sizes, I will use `Ctrl + D` to add a symmetrical layer. This layer will mirror the side panel, and we will create sewing lines to connect them. If you notice a smaller version appears, you can reduce its strength early on to make adjustments easier. ## Final Adjustments As we approach the final stages, I will make necessary adjustments to ensure that the fabric fits snugly against the virtual model. This includes lowering the surface diameter and the conflict thickness. Dragging the position of the board will help in visualizing the fit. ## Curve Adjustments Next, I found that the curve in the front was not ideal, so I'll adjust it using a round-shape curve tool. After making these adjustments, we can freeze this section before moving on to the upper part of the dress, where we will repeat the drawing and flattening process. ## Back Panel Creation For the back, we will draw a parallel board and deal with any wrinkles that may occur after sewing. Adjustments will be made to the lengths of the sides so that the panels fit well against the model's skin. ## Sewing the Panels Now, I will sew the back to the front in the 3D window, adding pins to prevent misalignment. After stretching the two front panels, we will check the overall fit to ensure it looks natural. ## Fabric Properties and Adjustments As we continue, I will change the fabric properties to better suit the design, including adjustments for leather material and other necessary changes. This will enhance the overall look and feel of the dress. ## Conclusion Thank you for your attention throughout this process. We have made significant progress on Hannah's dress, and I hope you learned valuable techniques for creating swimwear in Marvelous Designer. Feel free to join our QQ group if you have any questions or need further assistance.
